PAPERS.short: Agrawal Bihar low-cost sensor network ML exposure inequity short-term mortality 2026
PAPERS.title: Unveiling hidden air pollution exposure and impacts with low-cost sensor network-based frameworks.
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 from a dense statewide low-cost sensor network, gap-filled by machine learning
PAPERS.endpoint: District exposure by socioeconomic group; attributable short-term mortality
PAPERS.affil: Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur, India; Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur, India
PAPERS.n: Dense low-cost PM2.5 network across Bihar, fused with ML surfaces, NFHS socioeconomic data and India-specific relative risks. Northern districts carried 1.2 times the mean exposure of southern ones; district mortality per 100,000 varied up to 1.7-fold and daily attributable mortality 3.2-fold. State-level exposure inequity was limited, intra-regional inequity substantial. The abstract gives no sensor count, calibration R2/RMSE, or uncertainty on the attributable deaths, and the mortality is borrowed risk functions applied to sensor-derived surfaces, not an observed association; network calibration error propagates straight into the burden. Relevance: direct - the clearest flagship case for low-cost networks as a burden-estimation input outside cities.

PAPERS.short: Yang US claims case-control PM2.5 sinonasal malignant neoplasm 2026
PAPERS.title: Fine Particulate Matter Exposure and Sinonasal Malignant Neoplasm.
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 from NASA 1-km satellite-meteorology-land-use models, averaged to residential MSA over 6 months, 1 and 5 years
PAPERS.endpoint: First observed sinonasal malignant neoplasm diagnosis
PAPERS.affil: Stanford University, USA; Mayo Clinic Florida, USA
PAPERS.n: National commercial-claims case-control, 2007-2020: 3,600 SNM cases, 17,695 controls (~1:5). Per SD PM2.5 (about 2.5 ug/m3), adjusted OR 1.25 (1.05-1.49) for the 6-month mean, 1.31 (1.08-1.59) for 1 year and 1.36 (1.11-1.66) for 5 years, rising with averaging window. Exposure is assigned at metropolitan-area level, so a 1-km product is collapsed to an ecological contrast of ~0.2-0.3 ug/m3 between groups; smoking and deprivation are regional, not individual, and occupational wood/leather dust - the dominant SNM cause - is unmeasured. Cases are 10 years older than controls. Relevance: indirect - a rare endpoint where residence-level exposure from dense sensing would remove the MSA misclassification.

PAPERS.short: Zhang Shanxi 11-city time-series pollutant mixtures influenza vaccination 2026
PAPERS.title: Influenza Incidence in Relation to Air Pollution Mixtures and the Modifying Role of Vaccination in Shanxi Province, China.
PAPERS.pm: Daily city-mean PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, O3 from regulatory monitors
PAPERS.affil: Shanxi Medical University, China; Shanxi Medical University, China
PAPERS.n: 11 Shanxi cities, 2014-2022, DLNM with zero-inflated negative binomial and meta-analysis. Per 10 ug/m3 PM2.5, RR 1.024 (1.015-1.034); PM10 1.018 (1.010-1.025); NO2 1.115 (1.086-1.146). WQS (1.078, 1.005-1.157) and qgcomp (1.122, 1.064-1.182) mixture effects were driven by SO2 and NO2, not PM. Vaccination modification is city-level coverage, therefore ecological, and labelled exploratory. Surveillance incidence is care-seeking and testing dependent; 2020-2022 includes COVID-era behavioural shifts the abstract does not say were handled. Relevance: indirect - PM signal is small next to gases, which argues for multi-pollutant nodes rather than PM-only networks for infectious endpoints.

PAPERS.short: Hao Shanghai case-crossover lab-confirmed influenza six pollutants 2026
PAPERS.title: Association between short-term air pollutant exposure and influenza incidence in Shanghai, China: A case-crossover study
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, O3, CO interpolated by inverse distance weighting to individual address
PAPERS.affil: Sun Yat-sen University, China; Sun Yat-sen University, China
PAPERS.n: Laboratory-confirmed influenza cases, Shanghai 2013-2017, time-stratified case-crossover with IDW exposure at the individual level. Per 10 ug/m3 PM10, OR 1.019 (1.004-1.034); O3 was inverse (OR 0.959, 0.941-0.977). PM2.5, SO2, NO2 and CO were positive across lags but their point estimates are not in the abstract. Laboratory confirmation is the design's strength over syndromic counts; IDW from a sparse regulatory grid and selection into testing are the weaknesses, and the negative O3 term likely absorbs season. Read alongside the same-day Shanxi series: two independent Chinese designs give PM effects near 2% per 10 ug/m3. Relevance: indirect. \textsc{backfill}, entry 20 March 2026.

PAPERS.short: Kutzinski CAPNETZ air pollution sputum pathogen spectrum community-acquired pneumonia 2026
PAPERS.title: Air pollution is associated with a distinct pathogen spectrum in community-acquired pneumonia: a prospective multicentre cohort study.
PAPERS.pm: City-level PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO up to one month before enrolment
PAPERS.endpoint: Sputum pathogen detection and cell counts in CAP
PAPERS.affil: Universities of Giessen and Marburg Lung Center, Germany; Universities of Giessen and Marburg Lung Center, Germany
PAPERS.n: CAPNETZ, 4,446 CAP patients with sputum; pathogen found in 1,581, cell counts in 4,014. Mixed-effects logistic models: S. pneumoniae with SO2 (OR 1.75, p=0.008) and CO (1.57); E. coli with NO2 (2.75); higher PM2.5 with lower detection of the pathogen examined (OR 0.37, p=0.001). No CIs or increments in the abstract, so magnitudes are ungradable. City-level exposure over a month is coarse, many pollutant-pathogen pairs were tested, and an inverse PM2.5 association invites a sampling or antibiotic-pretreatment explanation the abstract does not exclude. Relevance: indirect - outcome definition, not exposure metrology, limits this.

PAPERS.short: Defrancesco lung-brain axis review PM2.5 Alzheimer disease mechanisms 2026
PAPERS.title: Mechanistic understanding of the role of the lung-brain axis in the pathogenesis of PM2.5-induced Alzheimer's disease.
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 (general; composition discussed as modifier)
PAPERS.affil: University of Technology Sydney, Australia; University of Technology Sydney, Australia
PAPERS.n: Narrative review positioning pulmonary injury, rather than direct translocation, as the main route from inhaled PM2.5 to AD pathology: systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, blood-brain barrier disruption and extracellular-vesicle signalling converge on amyloid, tau, microglial and autophagy-lysosomal dysfunction. Modifiers named are composition, co-pollutants, sex, APOE and epigenetic reprogramming. No search protocol, no quantitative synthesis; the framework is a hypothesis map and the human causal link remains epidemiological association. Relevance: indirect - if the pulmonary route dominates, deposited dose in the alveolar region, not ambient mass, is the exposure metric a sensor should be calibrated to serve.

PAPERS.short: Sun Waite review molecular mechanisms respirable silica coal dust asbestos lung disease 2026
PAPERS.title: Molecular mechanisms of dust-induced lung disease: exploring the role of physicochemical composition and cellular pathways.
PAPERS.pm: Respirable crystalline silica, coal mine dust, asbestos; reduced-iron minerals
PAPERS.endpoint: Pulmonary fibrosis and lung cancer mechanisms
PAPERS.affil: University of New South Wales, Australia; University of New South Wales, Australia
PAPERS.n: Review of respirable occupational dust toxicity: oxidative stress, mitochondrial and lysosomal damage, inflammasome activation, ferroptosis, necrosis and pyroptosis, macrophage/neutrophil activation and NK dysfunction driving fibrosis and tumorigenesis, with emphasis on silica and on coal dust bearing reduced iron. Covers antifibrotic and immunotherapy approaches. Narrative, no stated search or appraisal. The physicochemical angle (surface iron, crystallinity) is the useful part: it is why mass concentration alone mis-ranks hazard across dust types. Relevance: indirect - optical low-cost sensors are blind to mineralogy, so occupational dust monitoring needs composition or a source-specific mass-to-hazard factor.

PAPERS.short: Kumar firefighter occupational exposure neurotoxicity narrative review 2026
PAPERS.title: Occupational exposure and neurotoxic health effects in firefighters: toxicological mechanisms and health risks.
PAPERS.pm: Fireground combustion products: fine PM, PAHs, CO, HCN
PAPERS.affil: Tokyo University of Science, Japan; Tokyo University of Science, Japan
PAPERS.n: PRISMA-informed narrative review of literature to June 2026, without meta-analysis or risk-of-bias assessment. Proposed pathways: CO and HCN hypoxia with ATP depletion acutely; fine PM and PAHs reaching the brain, NLRP3 glial activation and ferroptosis chronically; heat, fatigue and sleep loss as amplifiers. The authors state the firefighter literature is mostly cross-sectional and the mechanisms come from non-firefighter models, so causality is uncertain. Relevance: indirect - fireground PM exposure is essentially unmeasured at the individual level; wearable PM sensing on turnout gear is the obvious gap.

PAPERS.short: Tan Shenzhen PMF-ML firework burning PM2.5 source apportionment 2026
PAPERS.title: Apportioning Firework Burning and Routine Source Contributions to PM(2.5) in a Chinese Megacity Using Two PMF-Machine Learning Frameworks.
PAPERS.pm: Hourly PM2.5 chemical constituents, Shenzhen, Jan-Mar 2023-2025
PAPERS.affil: Peking University Shenzhen Graduate School, China; Peking University Shenzhen Graduate School, China
PAPERS.n: Three Spring Festival seasons of hourly speciation in Shenzhen; PMF resolved 11 routine sources plus firework burning. Fireworks contributed 4.7% of PM2.5 over the full period, 33% during display episodes and over 50% at peak hours. Two ML surrogates (direct and indirect) reproduced PMF contributions and flagged fireworks as dominant during episodes. Agreement with PMF is circular validation - the ML learns PMF output, so it inherits PMF's factor ambiguity and no independent tracer test is reported. Relevance: direct for networks - episodic sources at >50% of hourly mass are exactly where a fixed humidity/composition calibration on optical sensors breaks.

PAPERS.short: Sathish Kanpur Mumbai nine-stage size-resolved aerosol chemistry ICRP deposited dose 2026
PAPERS.title: Size-resolved measurements matter for chemistry and health: paired inland-coastal size-resolved aerosol chemistry and the inadequacy of bulk PM(2.5) dose estimates.
PAPERS.pm: Nine-stage impactor PM (<0.43 to >9 um), ions and OC/EC; ISORROPIA-II pH and water
PAPERS.endpoint: Aerosol pH, SOC formation, ICRP 66 regional deposited dose
PAPERS.affil: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, India; Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, India
PAPERS.n: Paired Kanpur (inland IGP) and Mumbai (coastal) impactor sampling over three seasons. Fine mode (PM2.1) is up to 62% of mass in Kanpur, not Mumbai; Kanpur fine aerosol is more acidic (pH 3.5-4.5 vs 4.5-5.0). ICRP 66 dosimetry: fine mode delivers 53-75% of alveolar dose from 40-62% of mass, and Kanpur alveolar doses are 1.3-2 times Mumbai's. The authors flag that SOC-water associations lose significance at one value per sample day, and dose depends on assumed deposition fractions. Relevance: direct - a calibration fitted at a coastal site will misweight the inland fine mode that carries the dose.

PAPERS.short: Subramanian chamber size-resolved emission rates PM oxidative potential six indoor sources 2026
PAPERS.title: Size- and Time-Resolved Emission Rates of Particulate Matter Mass, Chemical Constituents, and Oxidative Potential from Indoor Sources
PAPERS.pm: Size-resolved PM mass, composition and DTT oxidative potential, <0.25 to 10 um
PAPERS.endpoint: Emission rates; respiratory-tract deposited mass and OP
PAPERS.n: Chamber tests of two incenses, candle, toaster, humidifier and cigarette. Emission was mostly unimodal and concentrated below 0.25 um, where mass-normalised DTT OP was highest; composition and OPm varied with size but little with time. 37 +/- 3% of emitted PM10 mass and OP is deposition-capable, 45 +/- 2% of it alveolar. For equal PM10 mass and OP, these indoor sources give an estimated 76 +/- 10% higher alveolar dose than ambient PM. Six sources in one chamber; the dose comparison is modelled, not measured. Relevance: direct - optical sensors undercount below ~0.3 um, so indoor nodes systematically miss the fraction carrying most OP.

PAPERS.short: Chen TRACER Houston micropulse lidar aerosol vertical profile boundary layer parameterisation 2026
PAPERS.title: Aerosol vertical distributions shaped by boundary layer dynamics in a coastal urban environment: insights from the TRACER campaign
PAPERS.pm: Aerosol concentration profiles from micropulse lidar constrained by surface aerosol measurements
PAPERS.endpoint: Aerosol layer depth and stratification vs boundary layer
PAPERS.n: Six months of TRACER (Houston, 2022) micropulse lidar retrievals anchored to ground aerosol data. An S-shaped fitting function yields an aerosol-layer depth and a stratification-strength parameter. Concentrations drop sharply at strong capping inversions, layer depth tracks boundary-layer growth and collapse, and sea-breeze passage swaps continental for maritime aerosol. Relationships with BLH and the potential-temperature gradient are statistically significant but weak (no r given). No health endpoint. Relevance: direct for satellite-surface fusion - the AOD-to-surface PM2.5 ratio depends on exactly this profile shape, and the parameterisation offers a physical predictor in place of BLH alone.

PAPERS.short: Ayittey Accra FRM gravimetric PM2.5 three sites e-waste 2021-2022 2026
PAPERS.title: Persistent urban PM2.5 pollution in Accra, Ghana: spatiotemporal patterns, meteorological and anthropogenic drivers, and associated health risks
PAPERS.pm: 24-h gravimetric PM2.5 by USEPA FRM samplers, >300 samples at three sites
PAPERS.affil: University of Ghana, Ghana; University of Ghana, Ghana
PAPERS.n: Two years (2021-2022) of FRM gravimetric PM2.5 at Adabraka (next to the Agbogbloshie e-waste burning area), Dansoman and Legon. All sites ran about 3-4 times the WHO 24-h guideline; Adabraka was highest at 60.76 (2021) and 60.54 ug/m3 (2022), with negligible interannual change but strong spatial contrast. PCA ties variability positively to temperature and negatively to RH. Hazard quotients exceeded 1 for adults and children. Sampling was intermittent (~300 samples over 3 sites and 2 years), and HQ applied to PM mass is a screening device, not an epidemiological risk. Relevance: direct - one of very few reference-grade West African series, usable to anchor low-cost and satellite calibration. \textsc{backfill}, entry 3 March 2026.

PAPERS.short: Gupta Maharashtra opencast coal mine PM2.5 composition oxidative potential 2026
PAPERS.title: Comprehensive assessment of PM2.5 exposures around a regional mining site in India: integrating chemical composition, oxidative potential and health risk
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 mass, EC/OC, metals, PAHs, OP (AA and DTT) at six sites
PAPERS.affil: IITB-Monash Research Academy, India; Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, India
PAPERS.n: Six sites around an active opencast coal mine in eastern Maharashtra: two roadside (~400 ug/m3), residential at 2 and 5 km (122 +/- 43 and 116 +/- 36 ug/m3), and background. Carbonaceous species and metals were ~40-50% of mass; Cr, Ni, Fe, Mg and Zn ran 5-10-fold higher near the mine. OPvAA and OPvDTT peaked roadside and correlated only weakly with metals and organics (r=0.3-0.5); regression explained 25-40% of OP. EC cancer risk ~1e-3 rests on a risk-assessment slope, not outcomes. Season and sample counts are not in the abstract. Relevance: direct - at this composition, optical-sensor mass calibrations from urban sites will not transfer. \textsc{backfill}, entry 25 June 2026.

PAPERS.short: Jaelani Surabaya Benowo landfill 15-min PM2.5 2020-2024 2026
PAPERS.title: The spatial impact assessment of landfill sites on air quality in Surabaya: a diurnal and seasonal perspective
PAPERS.pm: 15-minute PM2.5 at the Benowo landfill, 2020-2024
PAPERS.endpoint: Concentration trend and diurnal exceedance pattern
PAPERS.n: Only a one-sentence abstract is available. Five years of 15-minute monitoring at the Benowo landfill show PM2.5 rising from 37.17 to 50.32 ug/m3 between 2020 and 2024, 7-10 times the WHO annual guideline, with exceedance peaks at 07:00 and overnight. The authors attribute the timing to boundary-layer mixing rather than landfill operations. Instrument class, completeness and any upwind comparison are not stated, so landfill attribution cannot be judged. Relevance: indirect - the diurnal peak set by mixing depth is a reminder that a single fixed node cannot separate source from meteorology without a paired background site.

PAPERS.short: Ku North China Plain new particle formation GEOS-Chem-APM spring campaign 2026
PAPERS.title: Investigations of New Particle Formation Mechanisms in North China Plain during the Spring Campaign Based on Observations and Simulations
PAPERS.pm: Particle number size distributions; nucleation and growth rates
PAPERS.endpoint: NPF event occurrence and model skill
PAPERS.n: One-month 2016 spring campaign in an industrial North China Plain city: 10 NPF days, each after nighttime northwesterly ventilation under dry daytime conditions. GEOS-Chem-APM reproduced 6 of 10 events; NH3 was in excess; tripling H2SO4 raised nucleation but did not reproduce particle evolution, and simulated growth rates were 51% and 75% too low on well- and poorly-simulated days. Ten events and one season limit generality, and the campaign is a decade old. No mass or health metric. Relevance: indirect - NPF bursts raise ultrafine number with little PM2.5 mass, the regime mass-calibrated optical nodes cannot see.

PAPERS.short: Schwarz Helmholtz letter ultrafine particle health studies forest for the trees 2026
PAPERS.title: Letter to the Editor: Health effect studies of ultrafine air pollution-Are we missing the forest for the trees?
PAPERS.pm: Ultrafine particles
PAPERS.affil: Helmholtz Zentrum Muenchen, Germany; Helmholtz Zentrum Muenchen, Germany
PAPERS.n: Metadata only; a letter with no abstract, so no argument is asserted beyond the title. From the Helmholtz Munich epidemiology group (Schwarz, Pickford, Cyrys, Breitner-Busch), which runs long-term UFP number and size measurement in Augsburg. The title signals a critique of how UFP health studies are framed - plausibly metric choice (number vs surface vs size bins) or the pursuit of UFP-specific effects independent of correlated traffic pollutants. To be read when the full text is accessible. Relevance: possible - any UFP exposure standard decides what number-concentration sensors in a network should report.

PAPERS.short: Siddiqui narrative review AQI ASCVD South Asians 2026
PAPERS.title: Impact of Air Quality Index on Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Risk in South Asians: A Narrative Review.
PAPERS.pm: AQI and constituent pollutants (PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO, O3, NO)
PAPERS.affil: Aga Khan University, Pakistan; Aga Khan University, Pakistan
PAPERS.n: Narrative review arguing that worse AQI and its constituent pollutants raise ASCVD risk in South Asians, who already carry high genetic and metabolic predisposition, and that pollution may compound traditional risk factors. Reports no search strategy, no pooled estimate and no South Asia-specific effect sizes; it concedes that region-specific intervention evidence is thin. Using AQI as the exposure is the core weakness: it is a max-of-pollutants communication index, not a dose metric, and conflates PM with gases. Relevance: indirect - the region with the highest burden still lacks cohort-grade exposure, which is where dense sensing would add most.

PAPERS.short: Laban scoping review household backup generators emissions health Africa 2026
PAPERS.title: Health effects associated with emissions from household generators used for backup power in Africa: a scoping review.
PAPERS.pm: Petrol and diesel generator emissions: PM2.5, PM10, NOx, SO2, CO
PAPERS.affil: South African Medical Research Council, South Africa; South African Medical Research Council, South Africa
PAPERS.n: PubMed and Google Scholar scoping review; nine studies met inclusion, and only ~2% of screened studies addressed health outcomes directly. Generator emissions carried PM2.5, PM10, NOx and SO2 at high levels; reported links to respiratory symptoms, CO poisoning, and possibly cancer and hypertension rest on self-report, modelling or indirect evidence. No study established a causal link. Two databases, English only. Relevance: direct - generator plumes are intermittent, near-field and household-specific, a source that only distributed indoor/outdoor low-cost sensing can capture at the needed resolution in Nigeria, Ghana or South Africa.

PAPERS.short: US coal-fired power plant proximity Area Deprivation Index cross-sectional 2026
PAPERS.title: Distribution of Coal Power, Pollution, and Poverty.
PAPERS.pm: Proximity buffers (3, 10, 25, 50 miles) to operational coal-fired power plants; no measured PM
PAPERS.endpoint: Area Deprivation Index of neighbouring populations
PAPERS.n: 2023 Neighborhood Atlas and census block groups: 2,783,004 people (0.83% of the US) live within 3 miles of a coal plant, disproportionately in the most deprived ADI decile and more often American Indian/Alaska Native. The most advantaged decile had OR 0.04 (0.00-0.81) of living within 3 miles versus the most deprived - a CI spanning near-zero that signals sparse cells. Proximity stands in for exposure; no PM, metal or stack-emission data, and plant size and wind direction are ignored. Relevance: indirect - a siting map for fenceline nodes, not an exposure estimate.

PAPERS.short: Wang PM2.5 PM10 forecasting dual-data MWS-optimised ensemble learning 2026
PAPERS.title: PM2.5 and PM10 Concentration Forecasting Using a Dual-Data Strategy and MWS-Optimized Ensemble Learning
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 and PM10
PAPERS.n: Metadata only; no abstract in Crossref at issue time, so no finding is asserted. The title describes PM2.5 and PM10 forecasting from a dual-data input strategy with an ensemble learner tuned by an MWS optimiser. Carried because short-horizon forecasting is the step most networks attempt after calibration, and ensemble skill claims usually hinge on whether validation is time-blocked. To be assessed when the Elsevier abstract deposits: horizon, held-out period, skill against persistence, and whether sensor or reference data feed it. Relevance: possible, unassessed.

PAPERS.short: Hussain Bergin Pakistan smog episodes data-driven source attribution 2026
PAPERS.title: Attribution of Air Pollution Sources During Smog Episodes Across Major Urban Centers of Pakistan: A Data-Driven Approach
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time
PAPERS.pm: Smog-episode air pollution, likely PM2.5-dominated
PAPERS.n: Metadata only; no abstract in Crossref at issue time, so no finding is asserted. The title promises data-driven source attribution for smog episodes across several Pakistani cities; the author list includes Mike Bergin, whose group has built low-cost and satellite PM2.5 work in South Asia, and Muhammad Fahim Khokhar. Carried because Punjab smog is among the most extreme PM regimes, and attribution there decides between crop burning, brick kilns and traffic. To be assessed when the abstract deposits: data sources (sensor, reference, satellite) and method. Relevance: possible, unassessed.

PAPERS.short: Shankar meteorological drivers urban air quality weather-pollution interactions 2026
PAPERS.title: Understanding the Meteorological Drivers of Urban Air Quality: Weather-Air Pollution Interactions
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time
PAPERS.pm: Urban air pollutants (unspecified)
PAPERS.n: Metadata only; no abstract in Crossref at issue time, so no finding is asserted. The title points to an analysis, or possibly a review, of how weather variables drive urban air quality. Carried provisionally: meteorological normalisation is a prerequisite for interpreting network trends and for separating calibration drift from real change. Geography, pollutants and design are unknown, and it may be gas-dominated, in which case it will be noted as such in the weekly. Relevance: possible, unassessed.

PAPERS.short: Yao Harbin early-spring heavy pollution episodes natural anthropogenic drivers 2026
PAPERS.title: Natural and anthropogenic drivers of heavy pollution episodes in early spring in Harbin, Northeast China
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time
PAPERS.pm: Heavy-pollution episodes (PM2.5-dominated in Harbin early spring)
PAPERS.n: Metadata only; no abstract in Crossref at issue time, so no finding is asserted. The title sets natural against anthropogenic drivers of early-spring heavy pollution in Harbin, a period where heating-season combustion, agricultural residue burning and stagnant boundary layers overlap. Carried because cold, humid episodes are the regime where optical low-cost sensors overestimate most and where humidity correction matters. To be assessed when the abstract deposits: whether it separates open burning from heating and uses PM composition. Relevance: possible, unassessed.

PAPERS.short: Rogers VUV-AMS siloxane radical mass calibration source aerosol mass spectrometry 2026
PAPERS.title: Siloxane-Radical Species: Chemical Characteristics and Use for Mass Calibration in Aerosol Mass Spectrometry.
PAPERS.pm: Soot particles carrying vaporised PDMS siloxane oligomers
PAPERS.affil: University of Colorado Boulder, USA; University of Colorado Boulder, USA
PAPERS.n: Synchrotron VUV photoionisation aerosol mass spectrometry: heating conductive silicone tubing (150-230 C) inline with a soot source deposits siloxane oligomers on particles, producing three substituted-siloxane radical series and 21 recurring peaks between 73 and 799 Da. Calibration was verified on five PAHs (178-300 Da), 2,5-dimethylfuran and ethylene-pyrolysis hydrocarbons (165-374 Da). The radical-formation mechanism on the CuO target is hypothesised, not shown, and the method is specific to one research-grade platform. Relevance: indirect - siloxane from silicone sample lines is also a known artefact; the paper doubles as a warning for any sensor or sampler plumbed with heated silicone tubing.
